target: AArch64 QEMU virt with PCI VirtIO sound and WAV backend
command: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=/tmp/zeal-psalmody.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 scripts/check-compat.py --probe-psalmody
checks: The stock Psalmody editor opened, accepted a note, exercised playback, and exited with Shift-Escape.
The QEMU WAV backend captured 10,584 stereo frames at 44.1 kHz (0.24 s); channels matched, 7,938 left-channel samples were nonzero, peak amplitude was 7,000, and the measured note was about 392 Hz.
The graphical terminal recovered, 40+2 evaluated to 42, and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: This verifies Psalmody note playback through QEMU VirtIO sound and WAV capture. Audible output in live UTM or Raspberry Pi hardware remains unverified.
